findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher reads the wrong characters and inverts the comparison
findings.body: The new matcher is supposed to assert that the event's TOKEN_ID encodes the expected grant shortcut. The encoded prefix is 6 chars (2 for session type, 2 for token type, 2 for grant type), so the grant shortcut lives at indexes 4..6, but the code reads `items[0].substring(3, 5)` (e.g. for "onrtac" it extracts "ta" instead of "ac"). In addition the condition is inverted: `if (...equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` fails the match when the grant shortcut *does* match and passes when it does not. The net effect is that all the converted assertions (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) silently validate nothing about the grant encoding, so a regression in the encoding would go unnoticed; and if the extracted substring ever happens to equal the expected shortcut the tests would fail for a correct token.

findings.title: Null check for rawTokenId actually re-checks grantType
findings.body: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` duplicates the grantType check instead of validating `rawTokenId`. Consequently an `AccessTokenContext` can be built with a null raw token id, and `encodeTokenId()` will then produce an id like `onrtac:null` (string concatenation of null) which is silently written into the token's `jti`, instead of failing fast with a clear error at construction time.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
findings.body: `getShortcut()` is added as an abstract method to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` SPI interface. Any existing third-party/deployed grant type factory that does not implement it will no longer compile, and pre-compiled providers will throw `AbstractMethodError` at server startup, because `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` invokes `getShortcut()` on every registered grant factory. Providing a `default` implementation (e.g. returning null / a derived value) and handling the null case in the encoder would avoid breaking existing extensions.

findings.title: Public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) removed
findings.body: The copy constructor `public Context(Context context)` is deleted from the `OAuth2GrantType.Context` class in server-spi-private. Custom grant type implementations (or any code outside this repository) that create a derived context by copying an existing one will fail to compile / throw NoSuchMethodError after upgrade. If the removal is intentional it should at least be called out as a breaking SPI change; otherwise keep it and copy the new `grantType` field as well.

findings.title: Lazy grant/shortcut registration bypasses the duplicate-shortcut validation
findings.body: `getShortcutByGrantType()` and `getGrantTypeByShortcut()` lazily add entries to `grantsByShortcuts`/`grantsToShortcuts` without re-running the duplicate detection performed in `postInit()`. If a grant type registered later (e.g. a dynamically deployed provider) reuses an existing shortcut, the mapping is silently overwritten, so `getTokenContextFromTokenId()` will decode previously issued tokens to the wrong grant type. The duplicate check should also be applied on the lazy path (or the collision logged/rejected).

findings.title: Session type derived from clientSession.getUserSession() instead of the user session already available
findings.body: `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` dereferences `clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession()` without a null check. `TokenManager.initToken` already has the authoritative `UserSessionModel` as a parameter but does not pass it; for client sessions that are not (yet) attached to a user session this will NPE while building the access token, turning a token request into a 500. Passing the user session explicitly (or null-guarding and falling back to SessionType.UNKNOWN) would be safer.

findings.title: Access token jti format change is not documented / no upgrade note
findings.body: Access token ids (`jti`, and the `token_id` event detail) change from a plain UUID to `<6-char context>:<uuid>` (e.g. `onrtac:1f65761e-...`). This is an externally visible format change: clients, log pipelines or custom extensions that assume `jti` is a UUID (or that it contains no ':' character, e.g. when used in URLs or as a cache key) will break. The PR contains no documentation or upgrade/release note describing the new format and its stability guarantees.
